tone_statements.citation: Li Yunbing 李雲兵. 2003. 苗瑤語聲調問題 [Issues in Miao-Yao (Hmong-Mien) tones]. Language and Linguistics 語言暨語言學 4(4): 683-712. Taipei: Institute of Linguistics, Academia Sinica.
tone_statements.quote: 在苗語中，川黔滇方言貴陽次方言、惠水次方言、重安江次方言和湘西方言都沒有入聲調……沒有入聲調並不等於入聲調消失了，只是入聲調合併到別的調類中去了。貴陽次方言的擺托、惠水次方言的高坡都是 D1 調並入 C1 調，D2 調並入 A2 調 [p.702] … 苗語湘西方言西部土語如臘乙坪、貴陽次方言如擺托、惠水次方言如甲定、重安江次方言如楓香都是六聲六類 [p.706]
tone_statements.translation: Within Miao, the Guiyang, Huishui and Chong'anjiang sub-dialects of the Chuanqiandian dialect and the Xiangxi dialect all lack entering tones ... lacking entering tones does not mean they vanished, only that they merged into other tone categories. At Baituo (Guiyang sub-dialect) and Gaopo (Huishui sub-dialect) tone D1 merged into C1 and D2 into A2 [p.702] ... Layiping (W. Xiangxi), Baituo (Guiyang sub-dialect), Jiading (Huishui sub-dialect) and Fengxiang (Chong'anjiang) all have six tones in six categories [p.706].
tone_statements.locator: p.702, section 3.1 '苗語支語言 *-p、*-t 韻尾脫落導致的聲調合併', with Table 14 on p.703; and p.706, end of section 3
tone_statements.n_tones: 6 surface tones = 8 etymological categories with D1 merged into C1 and D2 into…

sources.note: Historical-comparative tone study across 26 Hmong-Mien lects with Jiading (Gaopo) as a datapoint: the Huishui sub-dialect has no separate entering (D) tones because at Gaopo D1 merged into C1 and D2 into A2 (Table 14 gives Jiading forms beside Dananshan, Baituo, Dapingjiang); counted by surface categories Jiading is '六聲六類' (six tones, six categories) although the etymological 8-category notation is retained; general discussion of tone splits by onset voicing/aspiration/prenasalization, mergers after loss of *-p *-t *-k, and 'tone fission' via prefix loss and sandhi.
